messages:
maria: Quick sync on the deferred-cutover approach we discussed in the RFC. I want to capture the open tradeoffs for eng-releases and get alignment on the safety nets.
ajay: TL;DR: prefer gradual cutover with a guarded stateful fallback rather than immediate full switch. fewer surprises in client sessions.
kai: Agree. One big question: how do we handle in-flight KV/cache mismatches during canary-to-primary switchover?
sasha: Two options I see: 1) keep sticky session affinity to the original target until session end, 2) do an async KV reconciliation and allow short-lived mismatch with error-tolerant clients.
maria: Right — affinity reduces complexity but harms balancing. Async reconciliation adds complexity to runtime and latency spikes.
oliver: For balancing, we could implement a fast-path router header: `X-Cutover-Phase: sticky|migrate` and let clients opt-in to migration. Internal SDK can default to sticky for 24h.
ajay: That header trick is neat. We should also decide what metrics drive automated rollback vs. automated ramp. example thresholds: 5xx rate > 0.5% OR latency p95 increase > 50ms for 5m.
kai: I'd add output-quality alerts — e.g., hallucination/regression score delta > 2% on the eval probe set. Quality telemetry should tie to the same rollback circuit.
sasha: On fallback semantics: do we failover to previous model variant, fallback to degraded compute (quantized variant), or route to a lower-SLO region? All valid but different cost/quality impacts.
maria: Proposal: prioritized fallback list per rollout config: [previous-stable, quantized-compat, backup-region]. Router picks first healthy. Health checks include: kube/infra health, token-error-rate, eval-probe pass-rate.
oliver: Implementation note: the router needs an API to query candidate variant compatibility. I suggest adding a lightweight capability matrix in the metadata store: `supports_streaming`, `max_sequence`, `kv_compat_hash`.
ajay: Also need to decide rollback policy for stateful features: if canary modifies KV layout, rolling back might require a migration step. For that, prefer canaries that are read-compatible first.
kai: Agree. Enforce read-compatibility in CI for any canary that touches persistence. If write-compatibility required, it must go through a two-phase migration with explicit manual approval.
deploy-bot: deploy starting: canary/1930001234 -> 2% traffic to us-east-1 pool. ETA 3m.
sasha: Ops question — who owns the fallback playbook? eng-runtime or eng-releases? I vote eng-runtime owns runtime circuit + health checks; eng-releases owns rollout config and thresholds.
maria: Sounds good. We should define the contract between them: a single JSON contract for rollout config (weights, thresholds, fallback_list, session_affinity_duration). Example: `{"weights": [2,98], "rollout_policy": "gradual", "affinity_s": 86400, "fallback": ["stable-v2","q8-compat","region-b"]}`
ajay: Make sure the contract is versioned. Changes to schema must be backward compatible.
oliver: For statefulness: session affinity enforced via a sticky cookie + router mapping. If we switch mid-session, SDK can request `migrate=true` to force transfer after a KV sync job completes.
kai: Edge case: long-running streaming sessions. We shouldn't force migration mid-stream. Add a 'drain' flow: new sessions go to target, existing ones remain until close or timeout.
sasha: QA and testing: add synthetic user journeys that simulate migration while validating outputs with canary prompt set. Add chaos tests that kill a fraction of canary hosts to ensure fallback is quick.
maria: Good. Timeline: we prototype router header + contract this sprint. eng-runtime to deliver capability matrix and circuit logic next sprint. eng-releases to nail the default rollout JSON schema.
ajay: One more thing — telemetry tag composition. All canary traffic must be labeled `rollout_id` and `variant_id` so dashboards can filter and alert.
oliver: I'll add that to the router PR. Also adding a light-weight preview endpoint for UX that shows active fallback priority for a rollout.
deploy-bot: deploy complete: canary/1930001234 at 2% -> success.
oncall-bot: oncall alert policy attached: `rollout-regression` (pager on call if rollback triggered).
maria: OK everyone, I'll write up these decisions in the RFC follow-up and add the rollout JSON schema. If anyone wants to add edge-cases, drop them here. :thumbsup:
